title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government has responded to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining its commitment to improving safety, transparency, and accountability in AI systems. It calls for new regulations, industry collaboration, and the development of public standards to ensure AI technologies serve the public interest.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: EU Regulation 2024/1689 establishes harmonised rules for the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence across the European Union to ensure safety, transparency and accountability. The government summary explains how the regulation amends existing laws and directives to create a cohesive legal framework for AI technologies.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is creating rules and guidelines to govern how artificial intelligence can be used in developing, marking, and delivering qualifications, aiming to keep the system trustworthy and fair. The policy clarifies what AI tools are allowed, how they must be monitored, and the responsibilities of exam boards and educators to protect students and employers.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report looks at how copyright laws affect the creation of AI systems. It evaluates the use of copyrighted works in training AI models and the implications for creators and users.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has responded to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency” by outlining its plan to strengthen AI regulation, boost innovation, and safeguard public safety. It commits to investing in research, improving oversight, and ensuring the benefits of AI are shared widely across society.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document explains what the AI and Public Standards Committee will do, its purpose, and how it will operate, including frequently asked questions for guidance. It serves as a practical reference for committee members and stakeholders on how to review AI’s impact on public standards.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission outlines CSPL’s perspectives and concerns to help shape the committee’s recommendations for AI regulation and policy.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explores how artificial intelligence is reshaping the regulation of medical products, highlighting the need for updated oversight that reflects AI’s unique risks and benefits. It advocates implementing the AI White Paper principles—such as transparency, accountability, and safety—to guide regulatory frameworks and ensure that AI-driven medical solutions remain reliable and trustworthy.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy sets out a vision for becoming the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI‑driven defence organisation for its size. It commits to responsible development, deployment, and partnership to strengthen national security and maintain a technological edge.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to use AI for improving services and boosting efficiency. It also outlines steps to identify, mitigate, and manage the potential risks that come with deploying AI in transport.
